hero.title: Undergraduate Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland in Switzerland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: **Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students** brings together engineering, biology, medicine, and technology for Indian students to create innovative healthcare solutions. The domain spans medical devices, diagnostic equipment, medical imaging, artificial organs, rehabilitation technologies, biomaterials and computer-assisted surgery. Switzerland has a strong research environment and a well-established medical technology sector, making it an attractive destination for students interested in health care innovation.

overview:
A key point is that dedicated Biomedical Engineering programs are more easily found at the master level than at the bachelor level. ETH Zurich offers a specialized MSc in Biomedical Engineering. The University of Basel and FHNW offer a joint master’s program. Before specializing, undergraduate students may also consider related degrees in electrical, mechanical, materials or life sciences engineering.

Students exploring **Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students** can compare university programs, eligibility criteria and specialization pathways with guidance from **Edu-Hawk Worldwide**.

faq.question: Is Biomedical Engineering possible for Indian students in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Yes. Indian students can apply if they satisfy the academic, language and other admission criteria of the institution they have chosen. Every application is considered on its own merits and admission is not guaranteed.

faq.question: Are there any bachelor programs in Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland?
faq.answer: There are fewer options for specialized master’s degrees than for dedicated undergraduate programs. Students should research associated engineering degrees and check the exact qualification and specializations available with each university.

faq.question: Is Biomedical Engineering taught in English at ETH Zurich?
faq.answer: ETH Zurich’s MSc in Biomedical Engineering is taught in English and consists of 120 ECTS credits. You must meet the academic and language entry requirements for the program.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee for studying Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Indicative budget: CHF 15,000-34,000 or more per year including tuition fees and living costs. The costs will depend on the university, city, accommodation and personal spending.

faq.question: What to do after Biomedical Engineering in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Graduates may find employment opportunities in medical device engineering, biomedical research, diagnostics, medical imaging, health care technology, quality assurance and research and development. Certain roles require further study or specialist skills or additional professional qualifications.
